text_or_cause: done; also --check, list, --help, --version, and empty input (zero frames, empty output)
suggested_pipeline_handling: continue

text_or_cause: usage: unknown option or command, bad --depth, missing --fps for a temporal effect, inexact --fps, a frame effect given --frames, frame larger than 2^32 bytes
suggested_pipeline_handling: stop before decoding (preflight catches these); report vfx's line

text_or_cause: effect, param or render: unknown effect, unknown or out of range param, unknown layer; at render time frame N: unsupported: ... or effect panicked
stdout_effect: temporal: nothing is written when the failure is at frame 0 (all input already spooled); frames before frame N stay written
suggested_pipeline_handling: report vfx's last stderr line; kill the encode or discard the partial file

text_or_cause: I/O: cannot open input or layer; input ends with a partial frame (N of M bytes) after K whole frames; write error (the reader went away: The pipe has been ended. (os error 109))
stdout_effect: frame effect: the K whole frames are written, then exit 4; temporal: nothing is written
suggested_pipeline_handling: treat a BrokenPipe on the vfx stdin as 'vfx ended' and read its exit status and stderr line instead of the pipe error

text_or_cause: not produced by vfx code paths read here; a crash or kill gives the operating system's status
suggested_pipeline_handling: treat as failure and print the number

text_or_cause: success; also given for: input that ends early (File ended prematurely), damaged data (decoder errors on stderr), an encode input of 5 whole frames and 100 bytes (Invalid buffer size ...), an empty encode input, and -n with an existing output (File ... already exists. Exiting.)
stdout_effect: frames written up to the damage
suggested_pipeline_handling: never take exit 0 as proof of a complete file: count frames and verify the output

code_or_variant: non zero, negative as i32 on Windows
text_or_cause: -2 for a missing input or output folder, -1094995529 for invalid data (mp4 without a moov atom), -542398533 for a libx264 open failure (odd width); Python on Windows reports the same status as an unsigned 32 bit number (3199971767 for the mp4 case)
suggested_pipeline_handling: map every non zero child status to the pipeline's failure code; print the number and the last stderr lines; do not pass it to process::exit on a platform that truncates to 8 bits

text_or_cause: ffmpeg or ffprobe ran and failed; Display is '<tool> failed (exit code N) while <context>:' plus the last 12 non empty stderr lines
suggested_pipeline_handling: failure; show Display

text_or_cause: a pipe operation failed; on Windows 'The pipe is being closed. (os error 232)' when ffmpeg ended without an error status (for example -n with an existing output)
suggested_pipeline_handling: failure; the cause is not in the text, so also report the encoder's stderr()

text_or_cause: ffmpeg or ffprobe not found; one line per place tried (explicit option, FFMPEG, PATH)
suggested_pipeline_handling: refuse to start; apply.py's list also has MEDIA_FFMPEG_PATH and the Windows install folders (R08)

code_or_variant: Error::UnsupportedPixFmt, UnknownPixFmt, InvalidSize, BufferSize, FrameMismatch, InvalidArgument

suggested_pipeline_handling: programming error or an unsupported size; report Display

text_or_cause: ffmpeg's stdout ended inside a frame while ffmpeg itself exited 0; not produced in any run here because ffmpeg writes whole frames
suggested_pipeline_handling: failure

suggested_pipeline_handling: pass the size or raise finish_timeout for large frames (R26)

text_or_cause: a bad flag, or {frames} used where the frame count is not known
suggested_pipeline_handling: fix the command line

suggested_pipeline_handling: report the message

suggested_pipeline_handling: report the stage name

text_or_cause: a stage ended inside a frame
suggested_pipeline_handling: report the stage name and the byte count
